english.title: Possess an offensive weapon in a public place
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) without lawful authority or reasonable excuse, had with you in a public place, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PUBLIC PLACE..), an offensive weapon, namely **(..SPECIFY THE WEAPON..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(1) of the Prevention of Crime Act 1953.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
without lawful authority/reasonable excuse
had with you in a public place an offensive weapon

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) There is a requirement to prove an intent to possess an offensive weapon - otherwise see H2215.
(ii) See section 1(4) for meaning of "public place" and "offensive weapon".
(iii) Note also that the intended use of the weapon may be by some other person.
(iv) See also offence wording H4431 for possession of offensive weapon on school premises.

welsh.welshlegislation: Yn groes i adran 1(1) Deddf Atal Troseddu 1953.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Four years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
